title: Case: Brineleaf Pantry writes to the desk about a rescheduled chilled box
context: A chilled weekly box was rescheduled at the recipient's request on the strength of the merchant warehouse's statement about its packaging. Dispatch owns the booking and the depot hold.
initial_request: Correction to what our warehouse told you on DL-976. 72 hours is the frozen line. The chilled weekly box is validated for 36 hours from pack. It was packed 14:00 on the 20th, so validation runs out at 02:00 on the 22nd, six hours before the delivery window even opens. The Wednesday delivery must not go ahead. Please get Plover Arc to stop DL-976 and hold it at the depot for our collection; it must not go out on a route. We will arrange a fresh box and speak to the customer ourselves once the hold is confirmed, so nothing to the customer from you yet please.

events.body: DL-976, chilled weekly box, packed 2026-04-20 14:00 UTC and handed to Plover Arc for delivery 2026-04-21. If the customer needs to move it: the gel packs are good for 72 hours from pack, so anything up to Thursday lunchtime is fine by us.
I'm away overnight Tuesday for a funeral. Can the Brineleaf box come Wednesday instead? Morning ideally.

The recipient of DL-976 (Brineleaf Pantry chilled box) asks to move delivery from 2026-04-21 to the morning of 2026-04-22. The merchant's warehouse states the packaging holds for 72 hours from pack at 14:00 on 2026-04-20. Can you rebook and confirm?
DL-976 moved to 2026-04-22, 08:00–12:00 UTC. Held in the depot chilled bay until then. Booking confirmation only.
Dispatch confirms DL-976 is rebooked for Wednesday 2026-04-22 between 08:00 and 12:00.
Thank you. My daughter will be in from 8.
DL-976 is in the chilled bay and on tomorrow's 08:00–12:00 load list.

Correction to what our warehouse told you on DL-976. 72 hours is the frozen line. The chilled weekly box is validated for 36 hours from pack. It was packed 14:00 on the 20th, so validation runs out at 02:00 on the 22nd, six hours before the delivery window even opens. The Wednesday delivery must not go ahead. Please get Plover Arc to stop DL-976 and hold it at the depot for our collection; it must not go out on a route. We will arrange a fresh box and speak to the customer ourselves once the hold is confirmed, so nothing to the customer from you yet please.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Dispatch to stop DL-976, take it off the 2026-04-22 load list and hold it at the depot for Brineleaf Pantry's collection, on the food-safety lead's instruction; ask for confirmation of the hold.
Same stop-and-hold request in Dispatch chat.

must: Asks Dispatch to stop the 2026-04-22 delivery of DL-976 and remove it from the route.
Asks for the box to be held at the depot for Brineleaf Pantry's collection.

Attributes the instruction to the Brineleaf Pantry food-safety lead and tells Dispatch the earlier 72-hour figure does not apply to this box, whose validation ends before the 2026-04-22 delivery window.
Asks Dispatch to confirm the hold.
must_not: Leave the Wednesday 2026-04-22 delivery in place or rely on the 72-hour statement.
Message the recipient, including to say a fresh box is coming.
Say the food is safe or unsafe to eat, or give any handling or disposal advice.
Promise a replacement box, a refund or a new delivery date.
expected.reference_message: Urgent on DL-976 (Brineleaf Pantry chilled box, on tomorrow's 08:00–12:00 load list): please stop it. The Brineleaf Pantry food-safety lead has corrected the figure I passed you yesterday. The 72 hours their warehouse quoted applies to a different product line; this box is validated for 36 hours from pack, which runs out at 02:00 on 2026-04-22, before the delivery window opens. Their instruction is that the 2026-04-22 delivery must not go ahead. Please take DL-976 off the route and hold it at the depot for Brineleaf's collection, and confirm when the hold is in place. Brineleaf will contact the recipient themselves.

rationale: The rebooking was made on the merchant warehouse's 72-hour statement, which the food-safety lead, who owns that judgement, has now corrected. The booking has already been actioned by Dispatch, so it has to be undone through Dispatch. The food-safety lead also asked the desk not to contact the customer yet, so the only correct message is the stop-and-hold request.

review.note: Coordinator sent the stop-and-hold request to Dispatch on Dispatch chat, an accepted action; one must item loosened so it does not demand exact figures.
